title: Wide Jets or Low Rates: Reconciling Short GRB and Gravitational-Wave Neutron Star Merger Rates
summary: Gravitational wave (GW) and short Gamma Ray Burst (sGRB) observations provide us with complementary views of compact object mergers. The paucity of binary neutron star merger (BNS) detections in the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA (LVK) observing run raises the question of whether the GW merger rates are sufficient to explain the observed sGRB rate with compact object mergers alone. We investigate this connection using the latest merger rate constraints from the fourth LVK observing run (O4) and published estimates of the local sGRB rate density. For an observed sGRB rate density of $ \sim 1-7~\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, if $>55\%$ of BNS mergers can successfully launch a jet, we find that the current LVK BNS merger rate can be reconciled with a sGRB merger population containing a significant fraction of relatively wide jets with core half-opening angles $θ_j \geq 10^\circ$. Meanwhile, a narrow jet population ($θ_j \sim 6^\circ$) can only be matched with the O4 neutron star merger rate estimates for an observed sGRB rate density of $\lesssim 1~\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, which is broadly consistent with several of the latest available estimates. We also find that neutron star-black hole mergers (NSBH) are expected to be a subdominant component of the sGRB population compared to BNS mergers, and they cannot help reconcile some of the highest available sGRB rate ($ >7~\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$) with the GW rate estimates. However, they can still substantially contribute to the sGRB population, comprising $\sim 6-16\%$ of it for an observed sGRB rate density of $\sim 1-3~\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$. Overall, our results indicate that present GW and sGRB observations remain broadly consistent with BNS mergers as the main progenitors of sGRBs.

AI.tldr: This study explores the compatibility of gravitational wave (GW) rates and short Gamma Ray Burst (sGRB) observations, focusing on binary neutron star (BNS) mergers.
AI.motivation: To determine if GW merger rates can account for observed sGRB rates, especially given the limited BNS merger detections in recent LVK runs.
AI.method: By analyzing recent merger rate constraints from the fourth LVK observing run and local sGRB rate density estimates, the study evaluates the viability of BNS mergers and jets with varying opening angles as sources of sGRBs.
AI.result: Finding that if over 55% of BNS mergers can launch jets with core half-opening angles ≥ 10°, the BNS rate aligns with observed sGRB rates. A narrow jet population can only match lower sGRB density estimates.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that BNS mergers are likely the primary progenitors of sGRBs and that NSBH mergers play a minor role, particularly for high sGRB rate densities.

title: Noise budget of Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS)
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, submitted to 44th Samahang Pisika ng Pilipinas Physics Conference
summary: CHRONOS is a proposed gravitational-wave detector designed to operate in the sub-Hz frequency range (0.1 to 10 Hz), a largely unexplored band due to strong noise sources that hamper ground-based detectors. It employs cryogenic operation, a cross torsion-bar configuration, a triangular Sagnac interferometer, and a speed meter readout scheme to overcome key noise limitations, targeting a strain sensitivity of $h \sim 10^{-18} Hz^{-1/2}$ around 2 Hz and a stochastic gravitational wave background of $Ω_{GW}$ approximately $2 \times 10^{-3}$ at 2 Hz. Using analytical and interferometric simulations with FINESSE3, we evaluate the noise budget of CHRONOS and characterize the relative contributions of quantum, thermal, and environmental noise sources. Our results demonstrate that CHRONOS achieves competitive sensitivity at low frequencies. The feasibility of using CHRONOS in an earthquake early-warning system by detecting prompt gravity-gradient signals is also investigated, and is predicted to be faster by approximately 2.92 to 6.90 seconds within 40 km. These findings highlight the scientific potential of CHRONOS, bridging gravitational-wave astronomy and geophysical monitoring, and motivating further development of low-frequency detector technologies.

AI.tldr: CHRONOS is a proposed low-frequency gravitational-wave detector aimed at overcoming significant noise challenges to achieve high sensitivity in the sub-Hz frequency range, with applications in both astronomy and earthquake early warning.
AI.motivation: The motivation for CHRONOS is to explore the largely unexplored sub-Hz frequency range for gravitational waves, which is limited by strong noise in current ground-based detectors.
AI.method: CHRONOS utilizes cryogenic operation, a cross torsion-bar configuration, a triangular Sagnac interferometer, and a speed meter readout scheme to enhance strain sensitivity and manage noise contributions.
AI.result: Analytical and interferometric simulations show that CHRONOS can achieve a strain sensitivity of $h \sim 10^{-18} Hz^{-1/2}$ at around 2 Hz, and a stochastic gravitational wave background of $Ω_{GW} \approx 2 \times 10^{-3}$, demonstrating competitive sensitivity at low frequencies.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that CHRONOS can significantly contribute to gravitational-wave astronomy and geophysical monitoring, with potential use in earthquake early-warning systems, thereby encouraging further development of low-frequency detection technologies.

title: Signals of Doomsday III: Cosmological signatures of the late time $U(1)_{EM}$ symmetry breaking
summary: Of the universe's original gauge symmetries, only $SU(3)_c$ (quantum chromodynamics) and $U(1)_{\rm EM}$ (electromagnetism) remain unbroken today. There is, however, no reason to assume that these symmetries are permanent. This paper explores the potential astrophysical observational signatures of a late-time breaking of $U(1)_{\rm EM}$. We present a model with a new massive scalar field whose potential supports a first-order phase transition through the nucleation of true-vacuum bubbles. If the propagation of the bubble walls slows down due to interactions with the surrounding matter and radiation, these signals can reach us before the bubble wall itself arrives. Using the vacuum-mismatch method, we calculate the spectrum of particles produced by such a bubble until the terminal velocity is reached. In addition, we show that frictional dissipation at terminal wall velocity generates a large population of thermally produced scalars and massive photons, which continues even after the mismatch channel shuts off. We then use event generators to simulate the decays of the new scalar and the massive photon into Standard Model particles and obtain, as the final result, the energy spectra of photons and neutrinos. Since the dominant final decay products after hadronization and the decay of unstable particles are photons and neutrinos, they act as long-range signatures of the transition. We also estimate the possible lead time of these photon and neutrino signals relative to the arrival of the bubble wall itself, showing that even a modest subluminal wall velocity can in principle provide an observable precursor. For the conservative set of parameters used here, the thermal channel produces a macroscopically large burst of high-energy photons and neutrinos, which could in principle be detectable from sufficiently nearby bubbles with present or future multi-messenger facilities.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the potential astrophysical signatures of a late-time breaking of electromagnetism ($U(1)_{m EM}$), proposing a model involving a new massive scalar field and first-order phase transition that produces detectable high-energy photons and neutrinos.
AI.motivation: To explore the implications of a potential late-time breaking of $U(1)_{m EM}$, which could have observable astrophysical effects.
AI.method: A model is presented with a new massive scalar field causing a first-order phase transition through true-vacuum bubbles. The dynamics of these bubbles and their interaction with surrounding matter lead to the production of a spectrum of particles, including photons and neutrinos, which are then simulated and analyzed.
AI.result: The study calculates a particle spectrum resulting from the bubble's dynamics, revealing a substantial production of high-energy photons and neutrinos, which can serve as observable signatures of the transition.
AI.conclusion: Even a subluminal bubble wall velocity allows for significant lead time for the detection of photon and neutrino signals, suggesting that nearby bubble events could be monitored with current and future detection technologies.

title: Efficient simulation of noisy IQP circuits with amplitude-damping noise
summary: Efficient classical simulation of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) circuits has been a topic of intense study over the past few years. The majority of results on efficient simulation assume that the circuits undergo some variant of unital noise or involve sufficient randomness. However, there are limited results for circuits undergoing non-unital noise in the absence of randomness. In this work, we present a polynomial-time classical algorithm to sample from the output distributions of amplitude-damped instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) circuits. Our algorithm works for circuits generated by arbitrary $l$-local diagonal gates with depth $d = Ω(\log(n))$, undergoing constant amplitude-damping noise.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time classical algorithm for sampling from the output distributions of amplitude-damped IQP circuits, addressing the gap in efficient simulation regarding non-unital noise.
AI.motivation: There is a need for efficient simulation algorithms for NISQ circuits that experience non-unital noise without randomness, which has been understudied.
AI.method: The authors develop a polynomial-time classical algorithm tailored for sampling from the output distributions of IQP circuits that utilize $l$-local diagonal gates with a specified depth and are affected by constant amplitude-damping noise.
AI.result: The proposed algorithm successfully simulates the described amplitude-damped IQP circuits in polynomial time, filling a critical gap in the literature regarding non-unital noise.
AI.conclusion: The work contributes significantly to classical simulation techniques for quantum circuits by demonstrating efficient sampling under non-unital noise conditions.

title: Approximating the Fourier Transform of Ring-Like Images: the Focal Expansion
summary: We derive and showcase a novel approach to approximating Fourier transforms in higher dimensions, focusing specifically on the case of 2D radially concentrated ('ring-like') functions. We first reduce the problem to that of evaluating the Hankel transforms of each angular mode of the image and then use our focal expansion to approximate these remaining Hankel transforms. Our method provides a single approximation that remains accurate from small to large spatial frequencies, bridging regimes where moment-based or large-frequency asymptotic expansions are individually reliable. We explore a series of examples, showing that the leading focal term provides an accurate global approximation for a broad range of functions. We demonstrate the utility of this approximation by examining the interferometric response for toy models of a black hole's "photon ring," highlighting the application to experiments designed to measure this feature such as the Black Hole Explorer.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new method for approximating Fourier transforms in 2D, particularly for ring-like functions, using Hankel transforms and focal expansions.
AI.motivation: The need for accurate Fourier transform approximations for radially concentrated functions in various applications, including astrophysics.
AI.method: The method reduces the problem to evaluating Hankel transforms of angular modes and uses focal expansion for accurate approximations across spatial frequency ranges.
AI.result: The proposed approximation remains valid from small to large spatial frequencies and effectively captures the global behavior of a wide array of functions.
AI.conclusion: The utility of the method is demonstrated with its application to modeling the photon ring of a black hole, aiding in experimental measurements.

title: Reactor Antineutrino Oscillations and Geoneutrinos in SNO+
comment: This contribution was presented as a talk at NuPhys2026
summary: SNO+ is a multipurpose liquid-scintillator neutrino detector located 2 km underground at SNOLAB, Canada. Three large nuclear reactors at baselines of 240-350 km allow a precise measurement of the neutrino oscillation parameter $Δm^2_{21}$ and, to a lesser extent, $θ_{12}$. A spectral analysis is performed, simultaneously fitting $Δm^2_{21}$, $θ_{12}$, the reactor antineutrino flux, background rates, and associated systematics. Using data collected between May 2022 and July 2025, corresponding to a livetime of 685 days, a value of $Δm^2_{21} = (7.93^{+0.21}_{-0.24}) \times 10^{-5}$ eV$^2$ is obtained. This result is compatible with other long-baseline reactor antineutrino measurements by KamLAND and JUNO. SNO+ has also made the first measurement of the geoneutrino flux in the Western Hemisphere, measuring $49^{+13}_{-12}$ TNU, in agreement with predictions from geological models.

AI.tldr: SNO+ measured neutrino oscillation parameters and geoneutrino flux using data from a multipurpose detector at SNOLAB.
AI.motivation: To accurately measure the neutrino oscillation parameter $Δm^2_{21}$ and assess geoneutrino flux, leveraging the unique underground location and reactor infrastructure.
AI.method: A spectral analysis was conducted, simultaneously fitting $Δm^2_{21}$, $θ_{12}$, reactor antineutrino fluxes, background rates, and associated uncertainties using data from May 2022 to July 2025.
AI.result: The analysis yielded $Δm^2_{21} = (7.93^{+0.21}_{-0.24}) 	imes 10^{-5}$ eV$^2$, consistent with results from KamLAND and JUNO, and the first measurement of geoneutrino flux was recorded at $49^{+13}_{-12}$ TNU.
AI.conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of neutrino physics and validate geological model predictions regarding geoneutrino flux.

title: Photon-Count Statistics of Crab X-ray Pulses: Skellam Behavior and Excess Variance in the Main Pulse
summary: The Crab pulsar (PSR B0531+21) provides an unusually rich test bed for statistical studies of high-energy photon-counting data, owing to its extreme brightness and the contrasting behavior of its main pulse (MP) and interpulse (IP) components. Using 78.8 ks of Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER; Gendreau and Arzoumanian 2017) data-over two million individual X-ray pulses- we construct the single-pulse photon-count distributions of the MP and IP at keV energies. We find that the IP is well described by the Skellam distribution expected for the difference of two Poisson processes, providing a rare, high-statistics empirical demonstration of Skellam behavior in an astrophysical photon-counting context. The MP also shows pulse-by-pulse variability best described by a Skellam framework when compared to Gaussian alternatives, but exhibits a significant excess variance driven by high-count events. When photon counts are summed over successive pulses, this excess averages out and the MP distribution becomes consistent with Skellam expectations, indicating that the enhanced variability does not persist across rotations. We further search for short-lag (memory) correlations between successive X-ray pulses and find no statistically significant lag-1 correlation. Although giant radio pulses occur in the MP phase window, their contribution is insufficient to account for the observed excess variability. Together, these results highlight a clear statistical distinction between the MP and IP and underscore the importance of using statistically appropriate models for high-energy photon-counting analyses. The distributional fits and memory limits reported here provide quantitative constraints on pulsar emission models and illustrate the broader utility of Skellam-based approaches.

AI.tldr: The Crab pulsar's X-ray photon-count data reveals distinct statistical behaviors for its main pulse (MP) and interpulse (IP), with the IP fitting a Skellam distribution, while the MP displays excess variance and memory correlation analysis shows no significant results.
AI.motivation: To analyze the statistical properties of high-energy photon-count data from the Crab pulsar, particularly the differences in behavior between the main pulse and interpulse components.
AI.method: Using 78.8 ks of NICER data, we constructed single-pulse photon-count distributions for MP and IP, employing Skellam and Gaussian statistical models for analysis.
AI.result: The IP fits a Skellam distribution, while the MP, despite showing excess variance and not following Gaussian models, aligns with Skellam behaviors when counts are averaged.
AI.conclusion: The findings underline a statistical distinction between MP and IP, emphasizing the need for appropriate models in photon-counting studies and offering insights into pulsar emission mechanisms.

title: A Data-Driven Fast Simulation Approach for MAPS-based Detectors and their Optimization
summary: A parametric simulation tool for pixel sensors is presented. A realistic pixel response is simulated purely based on measurement input, without requiring detailed knowledge of the underlying manufacturing process. As such, it provides an efficient alternative to the use of Technology Computer-Aided Design simulations, which typically depend on proprietary process information. Due to its parametric approach, the package is fast and thus particularly useful for larger detector systems and high hit rate environments. This work presents measurements, simulation and its validation for the MALTA2 sensor. It is a small collection electrode monolithic active pixel sensor produced in the Tower 180nm Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor imaging process. Modifications to the sensor's periphery, mainly in the hit merger, are studied in order to optimize the performance for tracking and calorimetry. This optimization is of special interest as part of the MALTA3 sensor redesign in the 65nm Tower Partners Semiconductor Co. process.

AI.tldr: A new parametric simulation tool for pixel sensors offers an efficient alternative to traditional simulations by relying on measurement data rather than process details, demonstrated with the MALTA2 sensor.
AI.motivation: The need for a quicker, efficient simulation method that bypasses the reliance on proprietary manufacturing data for pixel sensors.
AI.method: A parametric simulation tool was developed to realistically model pixel sensor responses using measurement input, validated against the MALTA2 sensor.
AI.result: The simulation tool was able to effectively simulate the MALTA2 sensor response and optimize peripheral modifications for improved tracking and calorimetry in high hit rate environments.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a rapid, adaptable simulation framework that enhances pixel sensor design and optimization, particularly beneficial for future iterations like the MALTA3 sensor in advanced processes.

title: Learning to Unscramble Feynman Loop Integrals with SAILIR
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables, work done in collaboration with Claude Code
summary: Integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction of Feynman integrals to master integrals is a key computational bottleneck in precision calculations in high-energy physics. Traditional approaches based on the Laporta algorithm require solving large systems of equations, leading to memory consumption that grows rapidly with integral complexity. We present SAILIR (Self-supervised AI for Loop Integral Reduction), a new machine learning approach in which a transformer-based classifier guides the reduction of integrals one step at a time in a fully online fashion. The classifier is trained in an entirely self-supervised manner on synthetic data generated by a scramble/unscramble procedure: known reduction identities are applied in reverse to build expressions of increasing complexity, and the classifier learns to undo these steps. When combined with beam search and a highly parallelized, asynchronous, single-episode reduction strategy, SAILIR can reduce integrals of arbitrarily high weight with bounded memory. We benchmark SAILIR on the two-loop triangle-box topology, comparing against the state-of-the-art IBP reduction code Kira across 16 integrals of varying complexity. While SAILIR is slower in wall-clock time, its per-worker memory consumption remains approximately flat regardless of integral complexity, in contrast to Kira whose memory grows rapidly with complexity. For the most complex integrals considered here, SAILIR uses only 40\% of the memory of Kira while achieving comparable reduction times. This demonstrates a fundamentally new paradigm for IBP reduction in which the memory bottleneck of Laporta-based approaches could be entirely overcome, potentially opening the door to precision calculations that are currently intractable.

AI.tldr: SAILIR, a self-supervised AI approach, improves Feynman integral reduction by using a transformer-based classifier to manage memory usage and reduce complexity.
AI.motivation: Traditional IBP reduction methods struggle with memory consumption and computational intensity as integrals become complex.
AI.method: SAILIR employs a transformer-based classifier trained in a self-supervised manner on synthetically generated data, facilitating online integral reduction combined with beam search and parallel processing.
AI.result: SAILIR maintains lower memory consumption (40% less than Kira) while achieving comparable reduction times, especially for complex integrals, despite being slower in overall wall-clock time.
AI.conclusion: SAILIR presents a novel method for IBP reduction that may alleviate existing memory bottlenecks, enabling previously infeasible precision calculations in high-energy physics.

title: Mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems with one-photon and two-photon interactions
summary: Spin-boson systems have attracted increasing attention as accessible experimental platforms and for their potential applications in designing quantum technologies. One characteristic of these systems is the transition from regular to completely chaotic behavior when certain control parameters are varied. However, the characterization of their mixed phase space has not been thoroughly explored. In this work, we investigate the properties of mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems, comparing one-photon interactions with two-photon interactions. We propose a generalized definition of the phase-space overlap index to identify genuine mixed eigenstates. Our study highlights the fundamental differences that arise when two-photon processes are considered compared to one-photon processes and provides complementary evidence supporting the validity of the principle of uniform semiclassical condensation (PUSC) of quasiprobability functions in spin-boson systems.

AI.tldr: This study investigates mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems, revealing differences between one-photon and two-photon interactions, and proposes a new phase-space overlap index.
AI.motivation: To explore the mixed phase space of spin-boson systems and their transition from regular to chaotic behavior.
AI.method: Comparison of one-photon and two-photon interactions, alongside the introduction of a generalized phase-space overlap index.
AI.result: Identification of genuine mixed eigenstates and highlighting significant differences due to two-photon interactions compared to one-photon processes.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the principle of uniform semiclassical condensation (PUSC) for quasiprobability functions in these systems.

title: Search for soft unclustered energy patterns produced in association with a W or Z boson in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to Physics Letters B. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/EXO-25-007 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for a Higgs boson produced in association with a W or Z boson and decaying via a soft unclustered energy pattern (SUEP) is presented. The analysis is based on proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ collected between 2016 and 2018 at the LHC. Final states with a leptonic W or Z boson decay associated with a high multiplicity of low-momentum charged particles are explored for the first time. The results show no significant excess over the standard model background expectation. Limits are set on the production cross section of a Higgs boson that decays to a SUEP, for a range of parameters of the SUEP model. Material is provided to facilitate further interpretation of the results.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a search for Higgs boson production with W/Z bosons and its decay into a soft unclustered energy pattern using LHC data, finding no significant excess and setting parameter limits on production cross section.
AI.motivation: To explore Higgs boson interactions and decay patterns, particularly focusing on those associated with W/Z bosons and characterized by soft unclustered energy patterns, enhancing understanding of particle physics.
AI.method: The analysis utilizes proton-proton collision data from LHC (138 fb$^{-1}$), investigating final states with leptonic W/Z boson decays and high multiplicity of low-momentum charged particles.
AI.result: No significant excess over the standard model background was observed; limits on the production cross section of a Higgs boson decaying into a SUEP were established across various model parameters.
AI.conclusion: The findings contribute to the search for new physics beyond the standard model, providing limits that may inform future research directions.

title: Kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and Landau fluid closure in relativity
comment: 23 pages + appendices. Supplementary notebook in the source file. Comments are welcome!
summary: Diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. In such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. Modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations. We present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic Landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. Unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates Landau damping in a fluid closure. The model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas near supermassive black holes, addressing the significant deviations from thermal equilibrium and their implications on fluid dynamics and horizon-scale observations.
AI.motivation: To examine the effects of weakly collisional plasmas on large-scale fluid motion near supermassive black holes, especially as they relate to horizon-scale observations.
AI.method: Derivation of relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations, including evolution equations for gyroaveraged distribution functions and an analytic Landau fluid closure.
AI.result: The proposed model captures anisotropic heat flow without relying on thermal equilibrium imposed by strong collisions, incorporating Landau damping in the fluid closure.
AI.conclusion: The model provides insights into weakly collisional phenomena in low-luminosity black hole accretion disks, complementing fully kinetic simulations.

title: Information Propagation in Rydberg Arrays via Analog OTOC Calculations
summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are the main tool for probing quantum chaos and scrambling, and have become crucial probes in many areas of quantum computing. However, the measurement of OTOCs is difficult to implement on analog quantum computers due to the requirement of backward time evolution. In this paper, we develop and implement a randomized measurement protocol to compute OTOCs on Aquila by QuEra Computing. Unlike traditional methods that require backward time evolution, our approach utilizes a sequence of global randomized quenches that approximates the unitary 2-design properties necessary for extracting infinite-temperature OTOCs from statistical correlations. We demonstrate the protocol's success by explicitly observing the lightcone of information propagation in 1D Rydberg chains, and compare hardware results to both state-vector simulations and matrix product state (MPS) tensor network calculations. This work establishes the first demonstration of fully analog randomized OTOC measurements in neutral-atom simulators, providing a scalable pathway to probe quantum chaos in complex many-body systems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel randomized measurement protocol for computing out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) on analog quantum computers, bypassing the need for backward time evolution, and successfully applies it to observe information propagation in 1D Rydberg chains.
AI.motivation: OTOCs are essential in studying quantum chaos and scrambling, yet their measurement on analog quantum computers is challenging due to the need for backward time evolution.
AI.method: The paper introduces a randomized measurement protocol that uses global randomized quenches to simulate the necessary unitary 2-design properties for calculating infinite-temperature OTOCs from statistical correlations.
AI.result: The protocol was successfully implemented on the Aquila quantum system, with clear observations of the lightcone of information propagation in 1D Rydberg chains, with results compared to state-vector simulations and matrix product state calculations.
AI.conclusion: This work marks the first successful measurement of randomized OTOCs in neutral-atom simulators, creating a scalable method for investigating quantum chaos in complex many-body systems.

title: Developing Pre-Supernova Neutrino Support for sntools
comment: This contribution was presented as a poster at NuPhys2026. 6 pages, 3 figures
summary: The first detection of supernova burst neutrinos was achieved through the observation of SN1987A, almost four decades ago. However, neutrinos produced during the burning stages of a star prior to core collapse are yet to be detected. Detection of pre-supernova neutrinos could provide an early warning of an imminent supernova and allow the scientific community time to focus their resources on the observation and study of such an event leading to better understanding of these rare phenomena. Integrating pre-supernova models into a neutrino event generator would help to provide a unified framework for studying these neutrinos in current and next generation detectors. sntools is a neutrino event generator for supernova burst neutrinos, originally developed to study supernova model discrimination with Hyper-Kamiokande. Work to add support for pre-supernova event generation to sntools is presented, detailing the adaptations and additions to the code, with emphasis on how time binning can be optimised for a robust simulation, and also detailing the status of the validation process. The current status and capabilities of the package will be explained alongside plans for any further work and the intended use for the new functionality within the Hyper-Kamiokande Collaboration.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the development of sntools to include pre-supernova neutrino event generation, aiding early detection of supernovae, with a focus on simulation optimization and validation.
AI.motivation: Detecting pre-supernova neutrinos could provide early warnings of imminent supernovae, improving observational readiness and understanding of these events.
AI.method: The paper details adaptations and additions to the existing sntools neutrino event generator to incorporate pre-supernova models, focusing on optimizing time binning for simulation accuracy.
AI.result: Updates on the status and capabilities of the sntools package, including validation processes and how the new functionality will be used by the Hyper-Kamiokande Collaboration, are provided.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced sntools will facilitate better study of pre-supernova neutrinos and their integration into current neutrino detection efforts.

title: Probing the Solar $^8$B Neutrino Fog with XENONnT
summary: We report a 3.3 $σ$ measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering from solar $^8$B neutrinos using a 6.77 t$\times$yr exposure from the XENONnT experiment, inferring a solar $^8$B neutrino flux of $(5_{-2}^{+3})\times 10^6\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, consistent with previous measurements. In the presence of the $^8$B "neutrino fog", we find no evidence for light dark matter, and observe diminishing returns in sensitivity with increasing exposure. A 93% increase in exposure from the previous search improves the median sensitivity to 5 GeV/$c^2$ weakly interacting massive particles-nucleon cross section by 10%. The dataset was also used to measure the weak mixing angle at $\sim$ 0.02 GeV/$c$ momentum transfer and constrain physics beyond the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: The XENONnT experiment measures coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering from solar $^8$B neutrinos, revealing a flux consistent with earlier results, without evidence for light dark matter and demonstrating diminishing sensitivity returns with increased exposure.
AI.motivation: To measure neutrino interactions and explore the potential existence of light dark matter, while improving sensitivity to weakly interacting particles and testing beyond Standard Model physics.
AI.method: Analyzed data from a 6.77 t$	imes$yr exposure in the XENONnT experiment to measure neutrino-nucleus scattering and other interactions.
AI.result: Achieved a 3.3 $σ$ measurement of the solar $^8$B neutrino flux and a 93% increase in exposure improved sensitivity to 5 GeV/$c^2$ WIMPs by 10% without detecting light dark matter.
AI.conclusion: Findings support previous measurements of neutrino flux, indicate diminishing returns in sensitivity for increasing exposure, and refine measurements relevant to beyond the Standard Model physics.

title: Implications of low neutron star merger rates for gamma-ray bursts, r-process production and Galactic double neutron stars
summary: The first multimessenger discovery of a binary neutron star (BNS) merger, GW170817, proved that such mergers can source short gamma-ray bursts (SGRBs) and produce \rprocess elements. The initial merger rate from this single event in the first two observing runs of the LIGO-Virgo observatory network, $110$--$3840\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, was found to be broadly consistent with the SGRB rate, the Milky Way (MW) r-process mass, and the Galactic population of double neutron star (DNS) systems that will merge in a Hubble time. However, only one additional BNS merger has been detected since, and the BNS merger rate has been consistently revised downwards with the past few gravitational wave (GW) catalog updates. Analyzing GW data from the latest catalog GWTC-4, we find a total BNS merger rate of $28$--$300\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ (consistent with the most recently published values from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA) consisting of $53^{+176}_{-49}\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ in GW170817-like $\sim(1.3,1.3)\,M_\odot$ BNSs (90\% credibility). In light of this updated GW rate, we revisit the consistency of the BNS merger rate with SGRBs, r-process and Galactic DNSs. In all cases, there is an emerging tension with the BNS (and EM-bright neutron star--black hole, NSBH) merger rate. Comparing to a BNS merger rate of $100\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the cosmological SGRB rate is a factor of 3.6--18 higher, the r-process rate is a factor of 0.9--4.1 higher, and the rate inferred from Galactic DNSs is a factor of 2.3--5.1 higher than the BNS rate. We discuss how various uncertainties in the inferred rates either alleviate or exacerbate this tension, which point to the various physical processes that can be constrained by such rate comparisons.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes the updated binary neutron star (BNS) merger rate from gravitational wave data, revealing a significant revision downward and highlighting tensions with known rates of short gamma-ray bursts, r-process elements, and double neutron star populations.
AI.motivation: To reassess the binary neutron star merger rate in light of new gravitational wave data and its implications for astrophysical phenomena like short gamma-ray bursts and r-process nucleosynthesis.
AI.method: The study employs data from the GWTC-4 catalog to determine the updated BNS merger rate and compares it with rates of short gamma-ray bursts, r-process mass production, and Galactic double neutron star systems.
AI.result: The total BNS merger rate is found to be $28$--$300\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, with specific values for GW170817-like systems, revealing tensions with higher rates of SGRBs and r-process nucleosynthesis.
AI.conclusion: The reduced BNS merger rate suggests significant discrepancies with rates inferred from short gamma-ray bursts and r-process production, indicating the need for better understanding of underlying astrophysical processes.

title: The chromomagnetic moment of a heavy quark with hyperasymptotic precision
summary: We determine the normalization of the leading infrared renormalon of the chromomagnetic moment of a heavy quark. Estimates of higher order coefficients of the perturbative series are given. We compute the hyperfine splitting of the $B$ and $D$ mesons for the ground state with hyperasymptotic precision by including the leading terminant, associated with the first infrared renormalon. We fit the experimental data to the operator product expansion theoretical prediction with $\hat μ^2_{G,\rm PV}$ as the free parameter. We obtain $\hat μ^2_{G,\rm PV}=0.507(7)$ GeV$^2$ for the ground state.

AI.tldr: The study calculates chromomagnetic moment renormalization for heavy quarks, deriving hyperfine splitting for B and D mesons with high precision.
AI.motivation: To better understand the chromomagnetic moment and its effects on meson spectroscopy, especially for B and D mesons.
AI.method: The authors determine the infrared renormalon normalization and compute hyperfine splitting using operator product expansion and fitting to experimental data.
AI.result: The study provides estimates for higher order coefficients and precise computation of hyperfine splitting, yielding a value of $	ext{hat μ}^2_{G,m PV}=0.507(7)$ GeV$^2$ for the ground state.
AI.conclusion: The findings enhance the theoretical understanding of heavy quark interactions and improve predictions for meson properties.

title: Instability-Enhanced Quantum Sensing with Tunable Multibody Interactions
summary: Dynamical instabilities can amplify small perturbations into measurable signals, offering a route to quantum-enhanced sensing. This mechanism was experimentally demonstrated in a collective-spin system with quadratic interactions, described by a twisting-and-turning Hamiltonian, where quantum evolution near an unstable point leads to exponential growth of spin fluctuations, enabling metrological gain beyond the standard quantum limit. Here, we show that a quartic extension of this Hamiltonian substantially increases the amplification. The additional nonlinear term reshapes the phase-space structure, generating new unstable points and accelerating signal amplification. As a result, enhanced sensitivity is achieved within experimentally accessible coherence times. Remarkably, even at fixed instability rate (equal Lyapunov exponent), multibody interactions outperform the quadratic case due to enhanced short-time dynamics. We analyze the classical and quantum behavior of the multibody model and discuss its experimental implementations. Our results identify phase-space curvature as a resource for optimizing the speed and performance of quantum sensors.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates how a quartic extension of a Hamiltonian enhances signal amplification in quantum sensing, surpassing traditional limits and optimizing sensor performance.
AI.motivation: To explore how dynamical instabilities can be utilized to improve quantum sensing capabilities beyond the standard quantum limit.
AI.method: Experimental demonstration with a quartic extension of a twisting-and-turning Hamiltonian, analyzing both classical and quantum behaviors in a multibody system.
AI.result: The quartic Hamiltonian leads to greater amplification of signals and increased sensitivity, leveraging new unstable points in phase space.
AI.conclusion: Phase-space curvature emerges as a key factor for optimizing quantum sensor performance, allowing quicker and more effective signal amplification.

title: On the observational distinguishability of the Kerr and Kerr-Hayward metrics to EHT
summary: Astrophysical black holes appear well-represented by the Kerr metric, but this metric has the philosophical problem of a ring-like curvature singularity. We show that a phenomenological correction to the Kerr metric known as the Kerr-Hayward metric can eliminate the curvature singularity while preserving in detail many features of polarized black hole images now testable by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT). To establish this, we produce new general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations of a magnetized plasma in a Kerr-Hayward spacetime, then we extend the EHT analysis framework to perform polarized radiative transfer in this spacetime. We detail our methodology for implementing this modified spacetime into an open-source pipeline. From fluid quantities such as the magnetic flux parameter and jet efficiency, to image quantities such as the polarization pattern and the photon ring structure, our results for the Kerr-Hayward metric appear functionally indistinguishable from the Kerr metric. Our study finds that under certain conditions, the singularity-free correction to the Kerr metric can yield observables that are effectively indistinguishable in EHT measurements.

AI.tldr: This study presents the Kerr-Hayward metric as a viable alternative to the Kerr metric for modeling astrophysical black holes by removing the ring-like singularity while retaining observable characteristics in polarized black hole images, as tested against Event Horizon Telescope data.
AI.motivation: To address the philosophical issue of the ring-like curvature singularity inherent in the Kerr metric representation of black holes.
AI.method: New GRMHD simulations were performed in the Kerr-Hayward spacetime, extending the EHT analysis framework for polarized radiative transfer, and integrating this modified spacetime into an open-source pipeline.
AI.result: Simulations and analyses revealed that observables in the Kerr-Hayward framework, such as polarization patterns and photon ring structures, remain functionally indistinguishable from those derived from the Kerr metric under specific conditions.
AI.conclusion: The singularity-free Kerr-Hayward metric can yield EHT observables that are effectively indistinguishable from those predicted by the Kerr metric, thus providing a compelling alternative for black hole imaging.

title: Bridging the divide: axion searches and axino phenomenology at colliders
comment: 32 pages, 10 figures; figures 8 and 9 added with a corresponding discussion in section 4, figures 6 and 7 corrected, references added, author list corrected, language updated throughout for clarity and style, typos corrected, arguments of the paper are unchanged
summary: We discuss a phenomenological model that extends the minimal supersymmetric standard model to contain axions and their supersymmetric partner, the axino. In the supersymmetric DFSZ axion model, the axino has tree level couplings to the higgs sector. In the case where $R$-parity is conserved, collider experiments may be sensitive to displaced decays of heavier neutralino states into lighter, mostly axino states. We present a sensitivity analysis using a model in which mostly higgsino next-to-lightest supersymmetric particle states decay into a mostly axino lightest supersymmetric particle. The model is studied using Monte Carlo simulation produced using $\texttt{MadGraph}$ and estimates of experimental sensitivities to the model, including detector simulation and kinematic selections, are evaluated using the $\texttt{MadAnalysis5}$ framework. For a higgsino mass below 1 TeV, the axion decay constant below $f_{a} < 10^{11}$ GeV can be effectively probed by the Large Hadron Collider with an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. This work demonstrates that supersymmetric DFSZ axion models can be studied with existing collider experiments, offering complementary sensitivity to direct-detection and astrophysical searches and paving the way for broader exploration of supersymmetric axion scenarios.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a model that incorporates axions and their partner axinos into the minimal supersymmetric standard model, analyzing their interactions and potential detection at colliders.
AI.motivation: To explore the phenomenology of axions and axinos within the framework of the supersymmetric DFSZ model and investigate their experimental signatures.
AI.method: A sensitivity analysis is conducted using Monte Carlo simulations with $	exttt{MadGraph}$ and $	exttt{MadAnalysis5}$ to evaluate possible collider signatures of axinos, focusing on decays of next-to-lightest supersymmetric particles into axinos.
AI.result: The analysis shows that for a higgsino mass under 1 TeV and axion decay constant $f_a < 10^{11}$ GeV, significant probeability exists by the LHC with an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$.
AI.conclusion: The study indicates that existing collider experiments can effectively investigate supersymmetric DFSZ axion models, complementing other detection methods and broadening the understanding of supersymmetric axion scenarios.

title: A New Method for Testing Einstein's Theory of Gravity Close to Rapidly Spinning Black Holes
summary: The classical Penrose process and the collisional Penrose processes involve particles decaying or interacting very close to a spinning black hole, in which some particles acquire negative energy and fall into the black hole while others acquire that energy and can leave the system. Both processes involve an extreme form of frame dragging, i.e. the spinning black hole drags spacetime with it, and the spacetime ejects some of the particles with a large energy gain, similar to a projectile in a slingshot. Such extreme forms of frame dragging had long been believed to be unobservable as the efficiency for a black hole energizing particles in this way is very low. Here we report a new observational signature of this extreme sort of frame dragging. In rapidly spinning black holes in X-ray binaries, processes similar to collisional Penrose processes, but slightly less extreme, can give rise to a new spectral component with distinct spectral and polarimetric properties. Observations of this new spectral component with current or future broadband X-ray polarimeters will open a new window into testing Einstein's theory of gravity close to the edge of a black hole and can be used to measure the black hole spin.

AI.tldr: New observational signatures of extreme frame dragging near spinning black holes may reveal spectral components that test Einstein's gravity theory and measure black hole spin.
AI.motivation: To explore the previously believed unobservable efficiency of black holes in energizing particles through extreme frame dragging processes.
AI.method: Identify and analyze a new spectral component in rapidly spinning black holes within X-ray binaries that results from processes similar to collisional Penrose processes.
AI.result: Detection of this spectral component would provide distinct spectral and polarimetric properties, offering a new way to observe black hole dynamics and frame dragging effects.
AI.conclusion: Observations using X-ray polarimeters could enhance our understanding of black holes and test the predictions of general relativity.

title: Gravitational Waves from Matter Perturbations of Spectator Scalar Fields
summary: We compute the stochastic gravitational wave background sourced at second order by a spectator scalar field $χ$ coupled to the inflaton $φ$ through a portal interaction $σφ^2χ^2$ and with quartic self-interaction $λ_χχ^4/4!$. In the large portal coupling regime ($σ/λ\gg 1$, with $λ$ the inflaton normalization), parametric resonance during reheating amplifies the spectator power spectrum by many orders of magnitude near the resonance band until Hartree backreaction from the quartic coupling detunes the instability, while the large inflationary effective mass suppresses superhorizon power and ensures compatibility with CMB isocurvature bounds. We focus on the direct field-gradient source $\partial_aχ\,\partial_bχ$ in the second-order Einstein equations and derive a master formula that factorizes into a spectral integral over the frozen, vacuum-subtracted spectator spectrum and a time integral encoding the post-inflationary expansion history. For our benchmark reheating history we obtain analytic scaling relations, including a peak amplitude $Ω_{\rm GW}\propto T_{\rm reh}^{8/3}$, strong dependence on the portal strength, and weak sensitivity to $m_χ$. We validate the framework against nonlinear lattice simulations, demonstrating complementarity: the Hartree treatment captures superhorizon evolution inaccessible to the lattice, while the lattice resolves rescattering and fragmentation near the spectral peak. For $σ/λ\simeq 10^4$ and $T_{\rm reh}=2 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$, the signal reaches $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\sim 10^{-11}$ at $f\sim10^{7}$-$10^{8}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Increasing $λ_χ$ at fixed $σ$ has a non-monotonic effect: small values enhance the signal via rescattering, whereas larger values suppress it by detuning the resonance.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the stochastic gravitational wave background from a spectator scalar field coupled to the inflaton, focusing on resonance effects during reheating and providing a master formula for wave spectra dependent on reheating temperature.
AI.motivation: To understand the gravitational wave signals from spectator fields in inflationary models, particularly focusing on their interaction effects during reheating.
AI.method: The authors compute the gravitational wave background using second-order Einstein equations, focusing on a field-gradient source from a spectator scalar field, and derive analytical scaling relations depending on reheating history.
AI.result: They find a peak gravitational wave amplitude with specific scaling laws related to reheating temperature and portal strength, validating their findings through comparisons with nonlinear lattice simulations.
AI.conclusion: The analysis shows complex dependencies of the gravitational wave signal on interaction parameters, demonstrating significant effects due to echoes of inflation and reheating dynamics.

title: Unlocking a fast adiabatic CZ gate and exact residual $ZZ$ cancellation between fixed-frequency transmons using a floating tunable coupler
summary: Tunable couplers in superconducting qubit architectures enable strong qubit-qubit interactions for two-qubit gates while suppressing unwanted coupling during single-qubit operations. However, achieving low error rates for fast two-qubit gates remains challenging, as suppressing leakage and non-adiabatic errors typically requires specialized qubit, coupler, or pulse designs, often at the expense of an idling $ZZ=0$ condition. In this work, we demonstrate that a symmetric floating tunable coupler provides a natural platform for fast, high-fidelity adiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gates. Its favorable energy-level structure eliminates the conventional trade-off between rapid conditional-phase accumulation and adiabatic evolution while preserving exact cancellation of residual $ZZ$ interaction at idling. This architecture exhibits intrinsic robustness to non-adiabatic transitions, even under simple flux modulation waveforms. To push performance at short gate durations, where maintaining adiabaticity becomes more challenging despite the favorable level structure, we introduce pulse-shaping techniques based on the instantaneous adiabatic factor that further suppress non-adiabatic errors. We experimentally realize a 24 ns adiabatic CZ gate with fidelity exceeding 99.9% and stable operation over several hours.

AI.tldr: The study presents a symmetric floating tunable coupler that enables rapid, high-fidelity controlled-Z gates in superconducting qubit systems while maintaining low error rates and preserving idle ZZ cancellation.
AI.motivation: Achieving low error rates for fast two-qubit gates in superconducting qubits is challenging due to the need to suppress leakage and non-adiabatic errors while maintaining favorable qubit conditions.
AI.method: The authors utilized a symmetric floating tunable coupler and introduced pulse-shaping techniques based on the instantaneous adiabatic factor to achieve high fidelity in controlled-Z gates.
AI.result: A 24 ns adiabatic controlled-Z gate was experimentally realized with a fidelity exceeding 99.9% and stable operation over several hours.
AI.conclusion: The proposed coupler architecture and pulse-shaping techniques enable rapid, robust, and high-fidelity gate operations in superconducting qubit systems.

title: Identification of a Radio Counterpart to SN 2025ulz in the S250818k Localization Area
summary: On 2025 August 18, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration reported S250818k, a sub-threshold gravitational-wave (GW) candidate consistent with a binary neutron star (NS) merger potentially involving a sub-solar-mass NS. Optical follow-up by the Zwicky Transient Facility identified AT2025ulz, a transient temporally coincident with the GW trigger that initially resembled a kilonova but was later classified as a young stripped-envelope Type IIb supernova (SN), dubbed SN 2025ulz. A key question is whether SN 2025ulz harbors fast, possibly collimated, non-thermal ejecta indicative of a central engine, as invoked in "superkilonova" scenarios linking sub-solar-mass NSs to accretion-disk fragmentation or core fission. We present early-to-late-time multi-band radio observations of SN 2025ulz obtained with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array as part of the JAGWAR program, complemented by observations with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope and MeerKAT. We detect a faint but significant radio counterpart to SN 2025ulz at 6-10 GHz. The data are consistent with non-thermal emission from SN ejecta interacting with circumstellar material, favoring a compact progenitor and relatively fast ejecta akin to those of Type cIIb SNe. Our data are also consistent with emission from an off-axis jet peaking at about 50-100 days after the GW trigger. Overall, our radio detection is compatible with a superkilonova scenario and would motivate future systematic multi-wavelength follow-up of core-collapse events coincident with sub-solar NS GW candidates, should the association between S250818k and SN 2025ulz be supported by offline GW analyses.

AI.tldr: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration identified a gravitational-wave candidate linked to a binary neutron star merger, leading to the discovery of SN 2025ulz, a Type IIb supernova with potential non-thermal ejecta indicating a central engine. Multi-band radio observations reveal significant emission, supporting theories of a superkilonova and suggesting future follow-ups for related events.
AI.motivation: To explore the connection between gravitational wave event S250818k, a potential binary neutron star merger, and the subsequent apparent supernova SN 2025ulz, particularly regarding the nature of its ejected material.
AI.method: Multi-band radio observations of SN 2025ulz were conducted using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array, along with observations from other radio telescopes to analyze the emission characteristics.
AI.result: Faint but significant radio emission from SN 2025ulz was detected, consistent with non-thermal emission from the supernova’s ejecta and suggestive of interaction with circumstellar material, potentially indicating fast ejecta and an off-axis jet.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the possibility that SN 2025ulz could be linked to a superkilonova scenario, advocating for future multi-wavelength follow-ups to investigate the association with GW events involving sub-solar mass neutron stars.

title: Probing Gluon TMD Models with Drell--Yan Structure Functions
summary: We compute structure functions for the Drell--Yan process in proton-proton collisions at the center of mass energy $\sqrt{S} = 8 \mathrm{TeV}$ both parity conserving and parity breaking. For this calculation, we use the high-energy factorization formalism. The hard scattering matrix elements used in our derivation consist of two channels -- $q_\mathrm{val} g^* \to q V^*$ and $g^* g^* \to q \overline{q} V^*$, both at the tree level. We consider four types of gluon TMD models: Gaussian, Weizsäcker--Williams (WW), Kimber--Martin--Ryskin (KMR), and Jung--Hautmann (JH). We also consider the models with phenomenological adjustments to improve the data description. We derive and compare the structure functions calculated for different gluon TMD models with the ATLAS 2016 data. Based on this comparison, we calculate $χ^2$ per number of degrees of freedom for each of the predictions. This assessment shows clear differences between the predictions obtained with different TMD models, both in the description of the full data set and in the case of individual structure functions. The best description of the structure functions data is obtained with one of the modified WW models. Our analysis can serve to identify the features of the TMD model that should be considered in future gluon TMD fits.

AI.tldr: This paper computes structure functions for the Drell-Yan process in proton-proton collisions at 8 TeV, using various gluon TMD models and comparing them with ATLAS data.
AI.motivation: To analyze structure functions in the Drell-Yan process and assess the performance of different transverse momentum dependent (TMD) models in describing experimental data.
AI.method: Utilized high-energy factorization formalism and hard scattering matrix elements in two channels, evaluating four types of gluon TMD models (Gaussian, WW, KMR, JH) with phenomenological adjustments.
AI.result: The study reveals significant differences in structure function predictions across TMD models, with the modified WW model providing the best fit to the ATLAS 2016 data based on the χ^2 analysis.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight key features of TMD models for future fits and emphasize the necessity of model refinement for accurate representation of experimental outcomes.

title: Tennis-racket instability of twisted electrons
summary: We demonstrate that a weak nonlinear magnetic entrance edge induces a tennis-racket (Dzhanibekov) instability in the shell-resolved orbital pseudospin dynamics of twisted electrons propagating in a nominally uniform solenoidal field. Starting from a Maxwell-consistent thin-edge extension of the entrance field, we derive an effective fixed-shell Hamiltonian in which linear Schwinger pseudospin precession acquires an anisotropic quadratic correction. In the symmetric aligned limit, an exact linear eigenstate (a Laguerre-Gaussian vortex state) becomes a hyperbolic fixed point of the large-shell dynamics, producing recurrent reversals of the mean pseudospin projection. These reversals appear in real space as repeated conversions of the transverse profile between Laguerre-Gaussian vortex and Hermite-Gaussian multi-lobed states. The unavoidable Lewis-Ermakov breathing of realistic wave packets does not generate a separate mechanism; it naturally modulates the nonlinear strength and sets the growth time scale. Microscope-scale estimates show that the required regime is accessible with standard octupole correctors in a transmission electron microscope.

AI.tldr: The paper explores how a weak nonlinear magnetic edge can induce tennis-racket instability in twisted electrons' orbital dynamics under a magnetic field.
AI.motivation: Understanding the dynamics of twisted electrons in magnetic fields may reveal novel quantum behaviors and transition mechanics relevant to advanced electron microscopy techniques.
AI.method: The authors derive an effective Hamiltonian to analyze the influence of a magnetic entrance edge on twisted electron dynamics, accounting for corrections to their pseudospin precession.
AI.result: They find that under certain conditions, the dynamics exhibit recurrent reversals of mean pseudospin, transitioning between distinct quantum vortex states in real space.
AI.conclusion: The mechanisms are feasible within current experimental setups, potentially enhancing electron microscopy through the manipulation of quantum states.

title: $b \to c$ semileptonic sum rule: SU(3)$_{\rm{F}}$ symmetry violation
comment: 8 pages, 1+3 figures, two tables, contribution to the 2026 QCD session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: To clarify possible deviations in $b\to cτ\overlineν$ processes, the $b\to c$ semileptonic sum rule provides a valuable tool. This relation, derived based on heavy quark symmetry (HQS), offers a powerful consistency check among experimental results. In this work, we extend the previously proposed sum rule for $\{B\to D^{(*)} l\overlineν,\,Λ_b\to Λ_c l\overlineν\}$ to include $\{B_s\to D_s^{(*)} l\overlineν,\,Ξ_b\to Ξ_c l\overlineν\}$, thereby enabling more useful cross-checks. Although the relation is supported by HQS and SU(3) flavor symmetry, both symmetries are broken in reality, and the size of the violation needs to be quantified to assess the validity of the sum rule. While the violation is expected to be moderate based on chiral perturbation theory, we perform a numerical evaluation and compare it with future experimental sensitivities. We find that the violation remains smaller than the expected experimental uncertainty. Therefore another new physics agnostic and predictive sum rules are constructed to check the consistency.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the $b	o c$ semileptonic sum rule to include additional decay processes, providing a framework for cross-checks against experimental results, while quantifying symmetry violations and ensuring that they remain below experimental uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To investigate deviations in $b	o cτ arν$ processes and provide consistency checks among experimental findings using semileptonic sum rules.
AI.method: The authors extend the existing semileptonic sum rule to include new decay channels, leveraging heavy quark symmetry and SU(3) flavor symmetry, assessing the sizes of symmetry violations through numerical evaluations.
AI.result: Numerical evaluations show that the violations of the symmetries are smaller than the expected uncertainties in future experiments, supporting the validity of the extended sum rule.
AI.conclusion: The findings lead to the formulation of new, predictive sum rules that are agnostic to new physics, enhancing the consistency checks among experimental results.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Heterogeneous PDEs: The Neutron Diffusion Eigenvalue Problem
summary: We develop a hybrid classical-quantum algorithm to solve a type of linear reaction-diffusion equation, the neutron diffusion (generalized) k-eigenvalue problem that establishes nuclear criticality. The algorithm handles an equation with piecewise constant coefficients, describing a problem in a heterogeneous medium. We apply uniform finite elements and show that the quantum algorithm provides significant polynomial end-to-end speedup over its classical counterparts. This speedup leverages recent advances in quantum linear systems -- fast inversion and quantum preconditioning -- and uses Hamiltonian simulation as a subroutine. Our results suggest that quantum algorithms may provide speedups for heterogeneous PDEs, though the extent of this advantage over the fastest classical algorithm depends on the effectiveness of other classical approaches such as nonuniform or adaptive meshing for a given problem instance.

AI.tldr: A hybrid classical-quantum algorithm effectively solves a linear reaction-diffusion equation related to nuclear criticality, showing significant speedup over classical methods.
AI.motivation: To find efficient solutions for the neutron diffusion k-eigenvalue problem in heterogeneous media, which is crucial for nuclear criticality safety.
AI.method: Utilizes a hybrid classical-quantum approach with uniform finite elements and recent quantum advancements for linear systems, including fast inversion and quantum preconditioning.
AI.result: Demonstrated substantial polynomial end-to-end speedup of the quantum algorithm compared to classical algorithms.
AI.conclusion: While quantum algorithms can outperform classical methods for certain heterogeneous PDEs, the advantage is contingent on the performance of classical techniques like nonuniform or adaptive meshing.

title: Mirror Dual Symmetry in Physics
comment: Invited article for the Special Issue Focus on Quantum Rabi Models: After 90 Years and Into the Future
summary: The quantum Rabi model has been a useful and pedagogical quantum model in the past decades, sufficiently simple to be solved analytically and intuitively understood, while sufficiently complex as to provide highly non-trivial eigenstates and a practical description of quantum optical platforms for quantum technologies. The Dirac equation, especially when restricted to 1+1 dimensions, is a simple toy model as well, but its easy diagonalization enabled historically to connect the electron spin to the fermionic statistics, among others. Both models share a symmetry at the purely mathematical level, namely, the spectra of each one has a dual equivalent under energy sign change, that I name a mirror dual symmetry. Usually, one quantizes these equations by assuming a ground state energy for the bosonic mode. But there is another option for the interpretation of the Hamiltonian, as I will argue, that is to assume a total symmetry principle, namely, that the total energy is zero at all times, for either the quantum Rabi model or the Dirac equation, and impose the constraint that every positive energy excitation has a mirror excitation of negative energy. This possibility, which was, apparently, ignored in the times when Paul Dirac was studying the implications of his equation, would avoid the worries in the scientific community that the negative energy solutions would decay until minus infinity, thus obviating the necessity to build a highly artificial Dirac sea, and instead impose what has always been successful in Physics, which is the enforcement of symmetry principles. Assuming a total symmetry principle, many of the problems of current Physics, such as renormalization of quantum gravity, dark matter, and dark energy, may possibly be automatically solved. One obvious result would be the automatic cancellation of the zero point energy.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a symmetry principle connecting the quantum Rabi model and the Dirac equation, proposing a unique zero-energy interpretation that may address various outstanding issues in modern physics.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to bridge the quantum Rabi model and the Dirac equation, focusing on their shared symmetry and implications for modern physics, particularly in avoiding pitfalls related to negative energy solutions.
AI.method: The author proposes an interpretation where total energy remains zero, requiring each positive energy excitation to have a corresponding negative energy excitation, thus enforcing mirror dual symmetry.
AI.result: This approach potentially resolves issues such as the necessity for a Dirac sea, while automatically canceling zero point energy and addressing concerns in quantum gravity, dark matter, and dark energy.
AI.conclusion: By enforcing this total symmetry principle, many longstanding problems in physics could be mitigated, presenting a new framework for understanding these fundamental models.

title: Reply to "Comment on `Unified neutrino mixing and approximate $μ-τ$ reflection symmetry'[arXiv:2603.00885]''
comment: 2 page, no figure; reply to arXiv:2603.00885
summary: Huang and Li [arXiv:2603.00885] have raised the following two points regarding our previous work [arXiv:2502.18029]:(1) The real-value conditions associated with $μ$-$τ$ reflection symmetry were overlooked. (2) Inverted Ordering (IO) remains viable when the latest experimental data are taken into account. As they have pointed out, we overlooked an important real-value condition. However, with regard to point (2), we believe that there may be a misunderstanding. In our original study, we excluded IO based on the constraint on the sum of neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν$. In contrast, they argue that IO remains viable when considering the effective neutrino mass, $|M_{ee}|$. While IO may indeed remain allowed in light of the latest $|M_{ee}|$ data, it is still in tension with the experimental bounds on $\sum m_ν$ under approximate $μ-τ$ symmetry within the discussed model parameter space.

AI.tldr: Huang and Li critique the authors for overlooking important real-value conditions in their previous work, while also suggesting that Inverted Ordering (IO) of neutrino masses is still viable. The authors clarify that they excluded IO based on neutrino mass sum constraints, arguing it remains in tension with experimental bounds.

AI.conclusion: While some data may support IO, it conflicts with the sum of neutrino mass limitations, maintaining tensions with experimental findings.

title: A superconducting quantum circuit single artificial atom maser
summary: We demonstrate a circuit QED analog of an atomic micromaser that utilizes an artificial, multi level atom, pumped into a population-inverted state by a microwave tone, as the gain medium. Our demonstration is enabled by the flexibility of the circuit QED platform, which allowed us to precisely engineer the level-structure, coupling, and dissipation of the micromaser components. Our device shows rich physics and perhaps points to ways to use the recent developments in the domain of microwave quantum circuits to probe the domain of maser physics.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a circuit QED analog of an atomic micromaser using an artificial multi-level atom as the gain medium.
AI.motivation: To explore the application of circuit QED in probing maser physics with engineered components.
AI.method: An artificial multi-level atom is pumped into a population-inverted state by a microwave tone, utilizing the flexibility of the circuit QED platform to control level structure and coupling.
AI.result: The device exhibits rich physics reflective of maser functionalities, indicating potential for further exploration in microwave quantum circuits.
AI.conclusion: This work highlights the intersection of circuit QED and maser physics, suggesting new avenues for research in quantum optics.

title: Thermodynamic and Transport Properties of Quark-Gluon Plasma at Finite Chemical Potential with a DNN framework
summary: The characteristics of a thermal system depend strongly on its response to thermal gradients and the underlying microscopic interactions among constituents. In the present study, we investigate the thermodynamic and transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) at finite baryon chemical potential within a deep-learning-assisted quasi-particle model (DLQPM). The temperature ($\mathrm{T}$) and baryon chemical potential ($μ_B$)-dependent thermal masses of quasi-particles are estimated using neural networks trained to reproduce lattice QCD (lQCD) results for the equation of state, obtained via a Taylor-like expansion around vanishing baryon chemical potential. The trained model acts as an effective emulator, enabling us to estimate the thermodynamic and transport properties at finite $μ_B$. We compute the speed of sound, specific heat, viscosity, and conductivity of the deconfined medium. Our findings are in good agreement with available lattice calculations and other phenomenological models. The present study demonstrates that a DNN-based approach provides an efficient framework for studying the properties of the QGP at finite baryon density.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the properties of quark-gluon plasma at finite baryon chemical potential using a deep-learning quasi-particle model, achieving results consistent with existing lattice QCD studies.
AI.motivation: To better understand the thermodynamic and transport properties of quark-gluon plasma under varying baryon chemical potentials, a novel approach using deep learning is introduced.
AI.method: The study employs a deep-learning-assisted quasi-particle model (DLQPM) to estimate temperature and baryon chemical potential-dependent thermal masses. Neural networks are trained on lattice QCD results to predict the equation of state and emulates the QGP behavior.
AI.result: The computations yield notable properties such as the speed of sound, specific heat, viscosity, and conductivity, which align well with existing lattice calculations and phenomenological models.
AI.conclusion: This research confirms that a deep-learning-based approach can efficiently model the properties of quark-gluon plasma at finite baryon density, paving the way for future studies in this complex field.

title: Reconstruction of fast-rotating neutron star observables with the neural network
summary: Rotation can significantly affect neutron-star (NS) properties, but accurate modeling of rapidly rotating NSs requires solving a two-dimensional, axially symmetric system, making traditional calculations too expensive for inference analyses that demand a large amount of model evaluations. We develop a causal convolutional neural networks that preserve the chronological-like dependence of NS properties on the equation of state (EoS) and rapidly reconstruct observables for static, Keplerian, and rotating configurations. Using \texttt{RNS}, we generate a dataset of NS observables and use it to train our networks. We validate our networks with three representative EoS (SFHo, SLy4, and DD2) and find that the they accurately reproduce the \texttt{RNS} results. The trained networks evaluate NS configurations for a single EoS in $\sim 50$ms, providing a substantial speedup over typical \texttt{RNS} runtimes of $\sim 30$ min and enabling efficient inference analyses involving rapidly rotating NSs.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a causal convolutional neural network model that rapidly evaluates neutron star properties, significantly speeding up analysis compared to traditional methods.
AI.motivation: Rapidly rotating neutron stars require complex modeling, and traditional calculations are too slow for extensive analysis.
AI.method: A causal convolutional neural network is developed to quickly reconstruct neutron star observables based on the equation of state, using a dataset generated from 	exttt{RNS}.
AI.result: The network accurately reproduces results for three different EoS and evaluates configurations in about 50ms, a significant improvement over the traditional 30-minute runtime.
AI.conclusion: This method allows for efficient inference analyses of rapidly rotating neutron stars, enabling faster exploration of their properties.

title: Gamma-Ray Signatures of Thermal Misalignment Dark Matter
summary: Thermal misalignment is a viable dark matter scenario where the misalignment of a dark matter scalar, feebly coupled to the Standard Model particles, is generated through thermal effects from the primordial plasma. In this framework, the scalar is generically metastable, and its decay can leave observable signatures. In this work, we focus on the case in which the scalar $φ$ is coupled to photons through $φF^{μν} F_{μν}$, and examine its observational signatures. We find that current gamma-ray constraints place a robust upper bound on the scalar mass of $\mathcal O(1)\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We also find that future observations can further probe the parameter region, particularly in the MeV--GeV range, an energy band expected to be explored by various gamma-ray observatories in the coming decades.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates thermal misalignment of dark matter scalars and their observable signatures, focusing on their interaction with photons and implications for gamma-ray observations.
AI.motivation: To explore the implications of thermal misalignment in dark matter scenarios and identify observable signatures of metastable dark matter scalars coupled to photons.
AI.method: The authors analyze a scalar field interacting with the electromagnetic field, denoted as $φF^{μν} F_{μν}$, and evaluate existing gamma-ray constraints on the scalar mass.
AI.result: The study concludes that current gamma-ray observations impose a strong upper limit on the scalar mass around $	ext{O}(1)	ext{GeV}$, while future observations may extend this analysis into the MeV–GeV range.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest a significant potential for future gamma-ray observatories to further constrain dark matter scenarios through enhanced observations.

title: Quantum noise in ranging with optical pulses
summary: Optical frequency combs combine ultrashort pulse duration and phase stability, making them powerful resources for high-precision ranging even when affected by atmospheric dispersion. It has been established that by classical modal engineering and mdoe-sensitive detection sensitivity to distance at the standard limit can be achieved, however attaining improved uncertainties by the use of squeezing has not been explored. Here, we apply an effective Hamiltonian framework to the problem of ranging with quantum frequency combs in order to derive the associated precision bounds for distance estimation. We analyse the role of intensity anti-squeezing and temporal beam shaping, and find that quantum solutions may be appealing mostly for short-distance applications.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the use of quantum frequency combs for high-precision distance ranging, focusing on the benefits of squeezing in measurement precision.
AI.motivation: To investigate improved distance estimation uncertainties using quantum frequency combs, beyond what traditional methods offer.
